subject: Mathematics

source.topic: Numbers, operations and relationships: Place value (numbers between 11 and 99)
source.subtopic: Decompose two-digit numbers into multiples of tens and units/ones to 75 (weeks 1-2), 80 (weeks 3-6) and 99 (weeks 7-10)

show.line: Eighty-four. Eight bundles of ten and four loose sticks. Eighty and four make eighty-four!

rounds.prompt: Seven bundles of ten and six loose sticks. How many sticks? Tap the number.

rounds.praise: Yes! Nine tens and two ones.

rounds.prompt: Sixty-eight. How many tens? Say the number.
Fifty and nine. Which number is it?
rounds.praise: Fifty-nine! Five tens and nine ones.

rounds.prompt: In the number eighty-seven, what is the eight worth?
rounds.praise: Yes! The eight is in the tens place. It is worth eighty.

rounds.prompt: Which number has nine tens and nine ones?
rounds.praise: Ninety-nine! Nine tens and nine ones.

rounds.prompt: Does the number have seven tens or eight tens? Put each card in its group.

hints: Count the bundles in tens. Then count on the loose ones.
The first digit is the tens. The second digit is the ones.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! I will break up ninety-six.
beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: Ninety-six is six tens and nine ones!
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! Ninety-six is nine tens and six ones.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's look together. Nine bundles of ten, six loose. Ninety-six!

parent_line: Can break any number up to 99 into tens and ones.
